shape: lib/ncd/catalog/schema.ts (briefing Appendix A). Keys named 'x' are outside the schema: provenance, lane and family, and proposed fields.

capabilities.display: Validated BP device with standard and large cuffs

sections.description: Reasons to test a person who does not have known diabetes.
What separates the types. Recorded, never inferred from build alone.
The measure, its date, and the target agreed with the patient.
Visual acuity, retinal view and grade.
Blood pressure, lipids, tobacco and cardiovascular risk.
When each routine check was last done.
What the person takes and what bears on its safety.

semantics.recorded: The `recorded` operator and every 'a result is already recorded' stop condition mean recorded AT THIS ENCOUNTER. A glucose from last month does not stand down the coma interrupt. Design B carries the time scope; the catalog grammar assumes the encounter's capture (fourth review, J19).
evaluator: J04: 'established_or_met' reads the non-pregnant criteria set as if pregnancy were answered, so an unknown pregnancy never hides a referral.
J16: an item switched off by `enabled: false` is reported as dark and nowhere else: not in fired steps, urgency, gaps, cautions or the pregnancy-withheld list.
J11: steps that ask for LESS treatment (`x.lessTreatment`) read every value, even one under a blocking caveat.
J25: a child (neonate, infant or child band) has pregnancy 'not possible'; no pregnancy question waits on her.
K14: a routine step that would fire but for a value under a blocking caveat reports that value as a named gap ('cannot be used for this patient'), instead of staying silent or reading it.
K11/K24: 'child' (pregnancy not possible) is the neonate, infant and child bands; the platform's child band ends before 10 years.
semantics.patientFacing: No catalog string is patient-facing. A surface without a restricted class shows `neutralDisplay` / `neutralAction` / `neutralAlternative` / `neutralProposal` and nothing else from that item (fifth review, K17).
semantics.interrupt: One interrupt per event: when several `immediate` rules are met, the surface interrupts once, headed by the first in `acuteOrder` (low glucose, then measured emergencies, then the clinical picture, then 'measure now' requests); a rule met only because pregnancy or a recent birth is unrecorded comes after every rule met on recorded facts. The interrupt carries every folded rule's action (`interruptActions`), so nothing is lost (seventh review, Q03, Q07).
semantics.pregnancyUnknown: Acute pregnancy rules (`pregnancyUnknownCounts`: 27D, 28, 28B, 28C, 28D, 28E) treat an unanswered pregnancy question, or 'not pregnant' with the weeks since a birth unanswered, as possible; they fire with the matching `unknownDisplays` entry (ask now, then the action) and name the gap. A rule with `unknownUrgency` fires at that urgency on the unknown path (28: an asymptomatic pressure asks the question the same day). Same-day pregnancy rules without symptoms wait for the answer (eighth review, T02, T08, T18).
semantics.targets: A target with `supersedes` replaces the targets it names when both would be proposed; an agreed tier decides. 'Avoid symptoms' proposes no HbA1c target by design (sixth review, L09).
semantics.diabetesContext: Every acute rule reads 'has diabetes' the same way: known diabetes, a recorded type, or any glucose-lowering medicine (sixth review, L04).
semantics.bands: An HbA1c control band is read only against a target that is actually proposed (`forTarget`), so a band never contradicts the target beside it (eighth review, T06).
semantics.caveatsEverywhere: A blocking caveat acts by direction on every rule and step outside the acute lane, on routine (not same-day or urgent) referrals and on targets; a value hidden by it is named as a gap only where it changed a met result. Acute rules and referrals for danger are never suppressed (N8; ninth review, U11).
semantics.riskModels: A risk model runs only when every feature in `mustHave` is recorded, and not when its `notWhen` holds; a missing input is never 'baseline' (eighth review, T13, T14).
semantics.adult: Age bands are effective bands: where a numeric age is recorded, under 16 is never 'adult' or 'older_adult' and 16 or over is never 'child' or 'adolescent', for rules, steps, flags and targets alike. A therapy flag shown under 16 shows its `under16Action` (refer; do not change the medicine here) instead of its action (ninth review, U07, U12). A recorded age of 10 to 15 is 'adolescent' even if the band says 'child' (tenth review, V16).
